newsitem.title: USA: Seitel sees more Yegua natgas output soon.
newsitem.headline: Seitel sees more Yegua natgas output soon.

text.p: Seitel Inc said Friday said it participated in a discovery in an Eocene Yegua natural gas zone in Texas which is expected to flow to sales next week.

This marks the 15th Yegua success in Wharton County, Texas -- about 60 miles southwest of Houston -- a program totaling 19 out of 27 wells completed to date, including five shallower Frio natural gas wells, a 70.4 percent success rate.

Seitel said the latest Yegua discovery, the Cox & Perkins Mitchell 1, was tested on an 9/64-inch choke and flowed 2.6 million cubic feet of natural gas and 114 barrels of oil per day. Flowing tubing pressure was 6,152 pounds per square inch.
Test production was from selective perforations at 8,798 to 8,832 feet; total depth drilled was 8,868 feet.

The Mitchell 1 well is expected to commercially produce at significantly higher rates than tested -- with stabilized flow anticipated to be 4 to 6 million cubic feet of natural gas and 200 to 250 barrels of oil daily, Seitel said.

The company owns a 20 percent working interest in the Mitchell 1. Other working-interest partners include privately-held Cox & Perkins Exploration Inc, the operator, 40 percent; Parallel Petroleum Corp, 20%; Domain Energy (formerly Tenneco Ventures), 10 percent; with unaffiliated individuals owning the remaining 10 percent.

"Our nineteenth Yegua prospect is currently drilling, with both another Yegua and two Frio prospects scheduled to spud in March, and further development drilling expected later in the year," said Seitel. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
